responsibility: Decode validates all segment/page access before x87 fetch/store; BT memory register indices require signed element displacement and effective-address-size wrap.

original_inability.x87: zfrsrvd.c invokes D_E08/D_E0a/D_E0e/D_E5e before F_/P_. Original usr_chk_word checks only two bytes. c_page.c vir_read_bytes/vir_write_bytes use contiguous physical reads/writes whenever the physical start is nonzero. At page offset FFC, sizes8/10/14/28/94/108 cross a page despite the initial word fitting. Different second-page mapping is never consulted; absent/read-only second page is not validated.
original_inability.rights: vir_* fallback uses supervisor spr_* operations. Setting only NO_PHYSICAL_MAPPING would not enforce user permissions on the second page; usr_chk_byte with original PAGE and CPL enforces them before effects. No buffer can span more than two pages at these sizes.
original_inability.segment: Original D_E5e checks94 for32-bit and106 for16-bit, whereas original F_E5e/P_E5e transfer108/94. The supported decoder itself supplies the contradictory lengths.
original_inability.bit: c_main.c OPERAND.sng is IU32; F_Gw/F_Gd load register values. Original unsigned shift yields8190 instead of-2 for word index FFFF and536870908 instead of-4 for dword FFFFFFFF. Original address_add supplies address-size wrap; raw += does not wrap16-bit effective addresses.

specific_diff_necessity.R0399: One shared decode macro validates final-byte access with original rights and selects original virtual transfer for noncontiguous pages. Removing this alone reintroduces unchecked/wrong physical access.
specific_diff_necessity.R0400_R0401_R0402_R0405: Each distinct original operand decoder passes its real8/10/14-or28/94-or108 byte span; unmodified decoders have no other whole-span check.
specific_diff_necessity.R0403_R0404: Correct two segment-limit operands to match original actual transfers. This is one combined replacement represented by insertion/deletion IDs, not independent features.
specific_diff_necessity.R0407_R0408: One expression each computes signed element displacement then calls original address_add. No new function or state; removing either restores wrong addresses for that operand size.
